title: He lied in the caliph's name to stop an execution | Folio 4 — The Honest Historian #Shorts
description:
And here the judge made a choice that could have cost him everything. He drew himself up and reminded Afshin who he was. Then he said that he carried a message from the caliph himself. And the message, as Beyhaqi gives it, was this. Do not kill al-Qasim. Do not touch him. Send him home at once, because your hand is short of him. And if you kill him, I will have you put to death in his place. There was no such message. The caliph had said nothing of the kind. The judge had just invented it, on the spot, in the caliph's name. Afshin trembled. He went pale, and almost fainted. Is this truly the caliph's message, he asked.

The full story: Folio 4: The Judge Who Lied to Save a Life — on our channel and on every podcast app.
